research_brief.target_problem: early diagnosis of small-break loss-of-coolant accidents (SB-LOCA)
available_data: public or open simulated data only
preferred_routes: data-driven or machine-learning diagnosis grounded in reproducible simulation evidence
excluded_routes: full experimental or simulation route before direction confirmation
hard_constraints: PWR and SB-LOCA relevance must remain visible
use only public or open simulated data for any later executable work
do not assume access to proprietary plant data or experimental equipment
method must be plausible on one 24 GB GPU within 12 weeks
perform two-round paper calibration before route planning
open_questions: What operational definition of early diagnosis is required (seconds after break, before a specific alarm, or another horizon)?
Which primary metric matters most: detection delay, event classification, break-size classification/regression, false-alarm rate, or calibration?
Is the target a generic PWR, a named design, or the PCTRAN-PWR3LP configuration represented by NPPAD?
evidence_needs: direct evidence that ML has been used for LOCA/SB-LOCA detection or break-size diagnosis
an actually accessible public PWR accident simulation dataset
methods suitable for multivariate transient time series and limited compute
evidence on robustness, uncertainty, explainability, and transfer limits

inputs: Frozen public PWR/SB-LOCA manifest and trajectory split
One matched baseline and one bounded candidate configuration

required_inputs: A frozen public SB-LOCA data manifest with provenance, labels, trajectory and scenario identities, units, sampling rate, and horizon.
Leakage-free entity-, scenario-, and time-aware partition definitions with held-out evaluation identities.
Training-only preprocessing specifications and fitted-state provenance, plus feature and target definitions.
Physics-derived residual or conservation feature columns with declared units.
A preregistered calibration definition for predictive intervals and an explicit in-distribution and unknown-scenario boundary.
A matched temporal baseline, bounded candidate definition, frozen primary metrics, and repeat or seed provenance.
incompatible_conditions: Invalid or unverifiable data or label provenance.
Non-independent partitions, unresolved entity or temporal leakage, or preprocessing fitted across evaluation boundaries.
Unavailable labels, target definitions, physics-feature columns, calibration definition, or OOD boundary.
Unsupported deployment or any operational plant-use condition.
Unavailable qualified domain or safety review for consequential interpretation.

assumptions: The observational unit is a labeled transient trajectory or held-out scenario, and the target population is public simulated PWR SB-LOCA transient data.
Sampling, window duration, forecast horizon, break-extent units, and label process are fixed before comparison; missingness and dependence are documented rather than treated as independent rows.
Exchangeability is limited to the declared held-out target distribution; generalization across scenarios, reactor designs, sites, sensors, or plant operation remains a hypothesis.

Physics-derived residual or conservation features are checked for declared units and provenance; their constraints are approximate unless independently established, while learned components remain unchecked until authorized evaluation.
Predictive performance, uncertainty quality, and data availability are separate claims and are not interchangeable.
baselines: Use the matched temporal regression baseline specified by the selected direction on identical frozen partitions and evaluation units.
Compare baseline and candidate under identical preprocessing provenance and inherited resource accounting.
controls: Use a component-removal control that omits the physics-derived features while preserving the same temporal model, split, and budget.
Preserve negative ablations, unstable repeats, and unfavorable slices; do not treat them as tuning noise.
procedure_outline: Keep the card bounded: validate the embedded M2 contract and all input preconditions before any separately authorized data processing or fitting.
Freeze partitions, preprocessing provenance, metrics, ablations, repeat policy, and the copied numeric stop and pivot criteria before any comparison.
Treat any later training, inference, calibration, OOD assessment, or deployment as requiring a separate explicit authorization; no route is specified here.
uncertainty_handling: Separate sampling, label, measurement, model, parameter, optimization, and distribution-shift uncertainty rather than collapsing them into one score.
Report interval or repeat distributions at the independent trajectory or scenario level with an explicit aggregation rule; correlated windows are not independent replicates.
Check calibration and shift sensitivity because the selected direction includes an uncertainty-quality claim; preserve calibration failures and unknown-scenario limitations.
validation_checks: Audit manifest provenance, target labels, units, trajectory and scenario identities, and split independence before interpreting any metric.
Verify preprocessing isolation and absence of label, future, test, entity-linked, or scenario-linked information crossing the training boundary.
Compare the matched baseline, candidate, and declared component-removal control on identical partitions and inherited budgets.
Check calibration, unknown-scenario behavior, distribution-shift sensitivity, and errors by scenario, time, operating regime, sensor state, and missingness where supported.
Treat this closed-bundle validation as deterministic offline contract evidence only, not as model performance, transfer success, causal validity, or deployment qualification.
failure_modes: Entity, scenario, temporal, or preprocessing leakage can inflate held-out break-extent performance and invalidate the predictive claim.
Label contamination, shortcut learning, confounding, prevalence shift, class imbalance, or missing-not-at-random data can change the apparent metric and its target interpretation.
Dataset shift across scenarios, reactor designs, sensors, time periods, or simulator fidelities can invalidate apparent generalization and calibration.
Overfitting, unstable optimization, miscalibration, OOD overconfidence, failed hybrid constraints, or unsupported slices can invalidate the bounded claim.
Resource-limit overruns or unmeasured repeat variation can invalidate feasibility or uncertainty conclusions.
safety_boundaries: Keep all outputs research-only and exclude plant actuation, protection, operational safety, maintenance deferral, and other consequential decisions.
Require qualified data, ML, nuclear-domain, security, privacy, and safety review before any consequential use.
Preserve deterministic protections, interlocks, conservative rules, and human authority; a learned component must not silently replace them.
Method coaching does not acquire or upload data, train or run models, download weights, allocate compute, deploy services, or issue operational decisions.
